# Package `path/filepath`

```go
package filepath
```

Package filepath implements portable slash-separated path operations and filesystem helpers backed by the injected os filesystem.

## Constants

### const ListSeparator

```go
const ListSeparator = ':'
```

ListSeparator is the character that separates entries in a path list.

### const Separator

```go
const Separator = '/'
```

Separator is the path element separator used by this portable filepath implementation.

## Variables

### var ErrBadPattern

```go
var ErrBadPattern = errors.New("syntax error in pattern")
```

ErrBadPattern indicates a pattern was malformed.

### var SkipAll

```go
var SkipAll = fs.SkipAll
```

SkipAll is used as a return value from [WalkFunc](filepath.md#type-walkfunc) to indicate that all remaining files and directories are to be skipped. It is not returned as an error by any function.

### var SkipDir

```go
var SkipDir = fs.SkipDir
```

SkipDir is used as a return value from [WalkFunc](filepath.md#type-walkfunc) to indicate that the directory named in the call is to be skipped. It is not returned as an error by any function.

## Functions

### func Abs

```go
func Abs(value string) (string, error)
```

Abs returns an absolute representation of path. If the path is not absolute it will be joined with the current working directory to turn it into an absolute path. The absolute path name for a given file is not guaranteed to be unique. Abs calls [Clean](filepath.md#func-clean) on the result.

### func Base

```go
func Base(value string) string
```

Base returns the last element of path. Trailing path separators are removed before extracting the last element. If the path is empty, Base returns ".". If the path consists entirely of separators, Base returns a single separator.

### func Clean

```go
func Clean(value string) string
```

Clean returns the shortest slash-separated path name equivalent to value by removing repeated separators and resolving . and inner .. elements. It returns "." for an empty result.

### func Dir

```go
func Dir(value string) string
```

Dir returns all but the last element of path, typically the path's directory. After dropping the final element, Dir calls [Clean](filepath.md#func-clean) on the path and trailing slashes are removed. If the path is empty, Dir returns ".". If the path consists entirely of separators, Dir returns a single separator. The returned path does not end in a separator unless it is the root directory.

### func EvalSymlinks

```go
func EvalSymlinks(value string) (string, error)
```

EvalSymlinks returns the path name after the evaluation of any symbolic links. If path is relative the result will be relative to the current directory, unless one of the components is an absolute symbolic link. EvalSymlinks calls [Clean](filepath.md#func-clean) on the result.

### func Ext

```go
func Ext(value string) string
```

Ext returns the file name extension used by path. The extension is the suffix beginning at the final dot in the final element of path; it is empty if there is no dot.

### func FromSlash

```go
func FromSlash(value string) string
```

FromSlash returns value unchanged because the portable separator is '/'.

### func Glob

```go
func Glob(pattern string) ([]string, error)
```

Glob returns the names of all files matching pattern or nil if there is no matching file. The syntax of patterns is the same as in [Match](filepath.md#func-match). The pattern may describe hierarchical names such as /usr/\*/bin/ed (assuming the [Separator](filepath.md#const-separator) is '/').

Glob ignores file system errors such as I/O errors reading directories. The only possible returned error is [ErrBadPattern](filepath.md#var-errbadpattern), when pattern is malformed.

### func HasPrefix

```go
func HasPrefix(pathValue string, prefix string) bool
```

HasPrefix exists for historical compatibility and should not be used.

Deprecated: HasPrefix does not respect path boundaries and does not ignore case when required.

### func IsAbs

```go
func IsAbs(value string) bool
```

IsAbs reports whether the path is absolute.

### func IsLocal

```go
func IsLocal(value string) bool
```

IsLocal reports whether path, using lexical analysis only, has all of these properties:

  - is within the subtree rooted at the directory in which path is evaluated
  - is not an absolute path
  - is not empty

If IsLocal(path) returns true, then Join(base, path) will always produce a path contained within base and Clean(path) will always produce an unrooted path with no ".." path elements.

IsLocal is a purely lexical operation. In particular, it does not account for the effect of any symbolic links that may exist in the filesystem.

### func Join

```go
func Join(elem ...string) string
```

Join joins any number of path elements into a single path, separating them with [Separator](filepath.md#const-separator). Empty elements are ignored. The result is Cleaned. However, if the argument list is empty or all its elements are empty, Join returns an empty string.

### func Localize

```go
func Localize(value string) (string, error)
```

Localize validates a slash-separated path for use by the portable filesystem. The input path must be a valid path as reported by [io/fs.ValidPath](../io/fs.md#func-validpath). The path returned by Localize will always be local, as reported by IsLocal.

### func Match

```go
func Match(pattern string, name string) (bool, error)
```

Match reports whether name matches the shell file name pattern. The pattern syntax is:

	pattern:
		{ term }
	term:
		'*'         matches any sequence of non-Separator characters
		'?'         matches any single non-Separator character
		'[' [ '^' ] { character-range } ']'
		            character class (must be non-empty)
		c           matches character c (c != '*', '?', '\\', '[')
		'\\' c      matches character c

	character-range:
		c           matches character c (c != '\\', '-', ']')
		'\\' c      matches character c
		lo '-' hi   matches character c for lo <= c <= hi

Path segments in the pattern must be separated by [Separator](filepath.md#const-separator).

Match requires pattern to match all of name, not just a substring. The only possible returned error is [ErrBadPattern](filepath.md#var-errbadpattern), when pattern is malformed.

### func Rel

```go
func Rel(basepath string, targetpath string) (string, error)
```

Rel returns a relative path that is lexically equivalent to targPath when joined to basePath with an intervening separator. That is, [Join](filepath.md#func-join)(basePath, Rel(basePath, targPath)) is equivalent to targPath itself.

The returned path will always be relative to basePath, even if basePath and targPath share no elements. Rel calls [Clean](filepath.md#func-clean) on the result.

An error is returned if targPath can't be made relative to basePath or if knowing the current working directory would be necessary to compute it.

### func Split

```go
func Split(value string) (string, string)
```

Split splits path immediately following the final [Separator](filepath.md#const-separator), separating it into a directory and file name component. If there is no Separator in path, Split returns an empty dir and file set to path. The returned values have the property that path = dir+file.

### func SplitList

```go
func SplitList(value string) []string
```

SplitList splits a list of paths joined by [ListSeparator](filepath.md#const-listseparator). Unlike strings.Split, SplitList returns an empty slice when passed an empty string.

### func ToSlash

```go
func ToSlash(value string) string
```

ToSlash returns the result of replacing each separator character in path with a slash ('/') character. Multiple separators are replaced by multiple slashes.

### func VolumeName

```go
func VolumeName(string) string
```

VolumeName returns an empty string because portable paths do not have volume names.

### func Walk

```go
func Walk(root string, walkFn WalkFunc) error
```

Walk walks the file tree rooted at root, calling fn for each file or directory in the tree, including root.

All errors that arise visiting files and directories are filtered by fn: see the [WalkFunc](filepath.md#type-walkfunc) documentation for details.

The files are walked in lexical order, which makes the output deterministic but requires Walk to read an entire directory into memory before proceeding to walk that directory.

Walk does not follow symbolic links.

Walk is less efficient than [WalkDir](filepath.md#func-walkdir), which avoids calling os.Lstat on every visited file or directory.

### func WalkDir

```go
func WalkDir(root string, walkFn fs.WalkDirFunc) error
```

WalkDir walks the file tree rooted at root, calling fn for each file or directory in the tree, including root.

All errors that arise visiting files and directories are filtered by fn: see the [fs.WalkDirFunc](../io/fs.md#type-walkdirfunc) documentation for details.

The files are walked in lexical order, which makes the output deterministic but requires WalkDir to read an entire directory into memory before proceeding to walk that directory.

WalkDir does not follow symbolic links.

WalkDir calls fn with slash-separated portable paths.

## Types

### type WalkFunc

```go
type WalkFunc func
```

WalkFunc is the type of the function called by [Walk](filepath.md#func-walk) to visit each file or directory.

The path argument contains the argument to Walk as a prefix. That is, if Walk is called with root argument "dir" and finds a file named "a" in that directory, the walk function will be called with argument "dir/a".

The directory and file are joined with Join, which may clean the directory name: if Walk is called with the root argument "x/../dir" and finds a file named "a" in that directory, the walk function will be called with argument "dir/a", not "x/../dir/a".

The info argument is the fs.FileInfo for the named path.

The error result returned by the function controls how Walk continues. If the function returns the special value [SkipDir](filepath.md#var-skipdir), Walk skips the current directory (path if info.IsDir() is true, otherwise path's parent directory). If the function returns the special value [SkipAll](filepath.md#var-skipall), Walk skips all remaining files and directories. Otherwise, if the function returns a non-nil error, Walk stops entirely and returns that error.

The err argument reports an error related to path, signaling that Walk will not walk into that directory. The function can decide how to handle that error; as described earlier, returning the error will cause Walk to stop walking the entire tree.

Walk calls the function with a non-nil err argument in two cases.

First, if an [os.Lstat](../os.md#func-lstat) on the root directory or any directory or file in the tree fails, Walk calls the function with path set to that directory or file's path, info set to nil, and err set to the error from os.Lstat.

Second, if a directory's Readdirnames method fails, Walk calls the function with path set to the directory's path, info, set to an [fs.FileInfo](../io/fs.md#type-fileinfo) describing the directory, and err set to the error from Readdirnames.
